candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: In D04 cells, siRNA knockdown of either NRAS or CRAF prevents the paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling induced by the BRAF inhibitor 885-A.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. Previous work had shown that activated RAS in melanoma signals through CRAF, while normal signaling in healthy melanocytes is accomplished through BRAF (Dumaz et al., 2006). To determine if CRAF was required for paradoxical pathway activation, Heidorn and colleagues treated D04 cells with siRNAs targeting NRAS and CRAF. This experiment will be replicated in Protocol 2.
candidates.notes: Registered replication protocol; no replication outcome is reported in this paper, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Drug-induced BRAF/CRAF heterodimerization in D04 cells requires active RAS signaling, because the RAS-binding-deficient CRAF[R89L] mutant does not bind BRAF.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. Since activated RAS is known to drive heterodimerization of BRAF and CRAF (Weber et al., 2001), Heidorn and colleagues also tested if drug binding drove heterodimerization of BRAF and CRAF, and if this heterodimerization was dependent on active RAS signaling. This key experiment will be replicated in Protocol 3.
candidates.notes: Registered replication protocol; no replication outcome is reported in this paper, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: In D04 cells, BRAF binds CRAF after BRAF inhibition, whereas the RAS-binding-deficient BRAF[R188L] mutant does not bind CRAF even in the presence of the inhibitor.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. The authors showed that BRAF binds to CRAF but only in the presence of WT RAS, not oncogenic RAS. This key experiment will be replicated in Protocol 4.
candidates.notes: Registered replication protocol; no replication outcome is reported in this paper, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Kinase-dead BRAF[D594A] binds CRAF, indicating that inhibition of BRAF activity rather than drug binding itself drives BRAF/CRAF binding and paradoxical MEK/ERK activation.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. After confirming that drug binding to BRAF drove BRAF binding to CRAF, Heidorn and colleagues tested a kinase dead version of BRAF (BRAF[D594A]) (Figure 4D). This key experiment will be replicated in Protocol 4.
candidates.notes: The paper labels this replication as Protocol 5 in the full text, although the introductory sentence refers to Protocol 4. Registered replication protocol; no replication outcome is reported, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
